findings.evidence: Lines 53–70: six `have`s with identical tactic scripts, used only in the final `simp` list at line 75.
findings.fix: Promote them to named lemmas in the `PauliMatrix` namespace (e.g. `toEuclideanLin_pauliMatrix_inr_single`), so the identity's proof is `Basis.ext` plus those lemmas and the column facts are available to later spin computations.
findings.issue: Six near-identical `have h00`–`h21` compute the action of `toEuclideanLin (pauliMatrix (Sum.inr i))` on `EuclideanSpace.single 0 1` / `single 1 1`, each by the same script `ext k; fin_cases k <;> simp [pauliMatrix, mulVec, dotProduct, Fin.sum_univ_two]`. This is general, reusable `PauliMatrix` API (the columns of σ₁, σ₂, σ₃ on `ℂ²`) hidden in a local block of a PhyslibAlpha-eligible module.

findings.evidence: Lines 74–76; by contrast every goal of this shape in SpinDecomposition.lean (e.g. lines 149–150, 192–194, 296–299) is `simp only [...]` then `module`.
findings.fix: Replace with `simp only [...]` and a closing `module` (the tactic used throughout `SpinDecomposition.lean` for exactly these smul/tmul goals), so the step is deterministic.
findings.issue: The identity is closed by `fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;> simp [9-lemma list] <;> abel` — a non-terminal full `simp` (not `simp only`) whose output feeds `abel` in four branches at once. Which branches reach `abel`, and in what normal form, depends on the ambient simp set, so an upstream simp-set change can silently break it.

findings.evidence: Lines 232–237; grep of `upstream/mathlib/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Trace.lean` for `trace_` shows no `TensorProduct.comm` lemma, so the fact is not available upstream and is worth naming here.
findings.fix: State it as a named lemma (trace of the exchange operator = `finrank`, or at least the `ℂ²` instance) next to the exchange identity, and prove it with an explicit `simp only`/`Finset.sum` computation rather than unfolding `Matrix.trace` in a full `simp`; `trace_spinSingletProj` and `trace_spinTripletProj` then just rewrite with it.
findings.issue: `hcomm` — the trace of `TensorProduct.comm` on `ℂ² ⊗ ℂ²` is `2` — is a reusable fact (Mathlib has no trace lemma for `TensorProduct.comm`; `Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Trace.lean` has `trace_tensorProduct`, `trace_prodMap`, `trace_one`, but nothing for the swap) hidden in a `have`, and proved by one opaque `simp [b, Matrix.trace, Fintype.sum_prod_type, LinearMap.toMatrix_apply]` that unfolds the `Matrix.trace` definition and relies on simp evaluating the `Basis.tensorProduct` repr of the swapped basis vectors.

summary: Proofs are mostly robust (module/norm_num, single simp only steps, no change/show). Two reusable facts are buried inside proof bodies — the action of the spatial Pauli matrices on the standard basis and the trace of the exchange operator — and the exchange identity closes with a non-terminal full simp feeding abel across four branches.
